findings.summary: The trace-writer, diagnostic reader, and healing orchestrator form a real code-backed observability stack with unit tests and concrete run artifacts.

The skill library, semantic retrieval, and Bayesian trust tracker are implemented and tested, but some top-level docs still describe the old 'skip after 5 successes' policy instead of the current Beta-Binomial posterior gate.
findings.required_correction: Update AGENTS.md and project-description prose to match the posterior-based trust gate.

findings.summary: ResearchAgent, VisualMonitor, VerificationGate, and BenchmarkEvaluator are real modules and are wired into operator/agent.py, but they are not universally enforced across all entrypoints and traced tests. Current prose often describes them as mandatory or always-on system properties.
findings.required_correction: Change repo-level wording from 'mandatory/always' to 'wired in the universal agent path and selected demos/tests' unless universal enforcement is actually added.

findings.summary: The architectural layering model is meaningful, but the current repo state no longer fully satisfies its own conformance gate. The strongest architecture-health claims should therefore be written as target-state or mostly-holds, not fully-holds.
findings.required_correction: Refresh architecture docs and/or repair the drift before claiming the layering model is currently enforced.

findings.summary: Most major cited papers and benchmarks are real and appropriate as direct or analogical support, but the repo does not consistently label when a citation is direct validation versus loose inspiration. Some newer references are credible but cross-domain (e.g. text-to-image or MCP tooling) and should be marked analogical. A few claims rely on citations that were not directly verified in this pass.
findings.required_correction: Adopt explicit labels: direct support, analogical support, speculative/proposed.

findings.summary: The sanitizer and credential-vault design are coherent for a macOS visual web agent, but several MCP-ecosystem benchmark and attack citations support analogous threat models rather than directly validating this exact local defense stack.
